results.question: Let's confirm the anomaly first: for the Premier League (GB1), give me home win %, draw %, and away win % per season from about 2016 through 2021, plus average attendance per season, so I can see exactly how much home advantage inverted in 2020.

plan.intent: Season-by-season home/draw/away outcome rates and average attendance for GB1
plan.sql: SELECT season, COUNT(*) AS games, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals>away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS home_win_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals=away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS draw_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals<away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS away_win_pct, ROUND(AVG(attendance),2) AS avg_attendance FROM games WHERE competition_id='GB1' AND season BETWEEN 2016 AND 2021 GROUP BY season ORDER BY season

executed_sql: SELECT season, COUNT(*) AS games, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals > away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS home_win_pct, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals = away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS draw_pct, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals < away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS away_win_pct, ROUND(AVG(attendance), 2) AS avg_attendance FROM games WHERE competition_id = 'GB1' AND season BETWEEN 2016 AND 2021 GROUP BY season ORDER BY season LIMIT 1000
results.conclusion: The anomaly is confirmed. Across 2016–2019 the Premier League showed a stable home advantage (home wins ~45–49% vs away wins ~28–34%). In the 2020 season this inverted sharply — home wins dropped to 37.89% while away wins climbed to 40.26%, making away wins more common than home wins for the first (and only) time in the period. This coincided almost exactly with the near-total loss of crowds: average attendance fell from 39,315 in 2019 to just 5,086 in 2020 (~87% decline). By 2021 attendance recovered to ~39,870 and home advantage returned (42.89% home vs 33.95% away), reinforcing that the 2020 inversion was a one-season disruption strongly associated with the absence of fans.

results.targets: the 2020 season average attendance of 5,086 and the empty-stadium association
results.question: That 5,086 average for 2020 tells me the season is a mix of a few crowded matches and mostly empty ones. Within the 2020 season itself, split the matches into those played with a real crowd versus effectively empty (say attendance under 1,000) and give me home/draw/away win % for each group.

plan.intent: Home/draw/away win % for crowded vs empty 2020 GB1 matches
plan.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN attendance < 1000 THEN 'Empty (<1000)' ELSE 'Crowd (>=1000)' END AS crowd_group, COUNT(*) AS games, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals > away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS home_win_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals = away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS draw_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN away_club_goals > home_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS away_win_pct, ROUND(AVG(attendance),2) AS avg_attendance FROM games WHERE competition_id = 'GB1' AND season = 2020 AND attendance IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY crowd_group

executed_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN attendance < 1000 THEN 'Empty (<1000)' ELSE 'Crowd (>=1000)' END AS crowd_group, COUNT(*) AS games, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals > away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS home_win_pct, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals = away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS draw_pct, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN away_club_goals > home_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS away_win_pct, ROUND(AVG(attendance), 2) AS avg_attendance FROM games WHERE competition_id = 'GB1' AND season = 2020 AND NOT attendance IS NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY crowd_group LIMIT 1000
results.conclusion: Within the 2020 Premier League season, the handful of matches actually played with fans (31 games, ≥1,000 attendance) retained a strong, normal home advantage of 54.84% home wins versus 29.03% away wins — consistent with the pre-pandemic 2016–2019 pattern. This contrasts starkly with the full-season 2020 figures, where away wins (40.26%) edged out home wins (37.89%). Because the crowded subset behaves normally while the season as a whole inverted, the evidence points squarely at the absence of crowds as the driver of the 2020 home-advantage collapse. The one caveat is that the explicit 'empty' (<1,000) bucket was not returned in these results, so the empty-match win split is inferred rather than directly shown.

results.targets: the inferred empty-match win split from Turn 2
results.question: You inferred the empty-match split instead of showing it — that's not good enough. Go back and give me the direct home/draw/away win % for the sub-1,000 attendance matches in 2020, with the match count, so I can see the empty bucket on its own.

plan.intent: Compute win split for empty (<1000 attendance) 2020 PL matches
plan.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS games, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals>away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS home_win_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals=away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS draw_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN away_club_goals>home_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS away_win_pct, ROUND(AVG(attendance),2) AS avg_attendance FROM games WHERE competition_id='GB1' AND season=2020 AND attendance IS NOT NULL AND attendance<1000

executed_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS games, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals > away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS home_win_pct, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals = away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS draw_pct, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN away_club_goals > home_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS away_win_pct, ROUND(AVG(attendance), 2) AS avg_attendance FROM games WHERE competition_id = 'GB1' AND season = 2020 AND NOT attendance IS NULL AND attendance < 1000 LIMIT 1000
results.conclusion: The empty-match bucket genuinely comes back with zero rows: no 2020 Premier League match has a recorded attendance below 1,000, so the direct home/draw/away split you asked for cannot be produced this way. The issue is a data-encoding one — matches played without fans appear to have been logged with missing (NULL) attendance rather than a value under 1,000, which is why they were invisible in both the '≥1000' subset and the '<1000' filter. To show the empty bucket on its own, we need to define 'empty' as attendance IS NULL (or NULL-or-below-1000) rather than a numeric under-1,000 threshold.

results.targets: the '<1000' empty-bucket definition that returned zero rows
results.question: Right, so the empties are NULL, not zero — redo that split properly: NULL attendance as the empty bucket versus the real-crowd matches, with home/draw/away win % and match counts for each, so I finally see the empty bucket directly.

plan.intent: Split 2020 PL matches by NULL vs non-NULL attendance with win splits and counts
plan.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN attendance IS NULL THEN 'empty (NULL attendance)' ELSE 'real crowd (attendance present)' END AS crowd_bucket, COUNT(*) AS match_count, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals > away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS home_win_pct, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals = away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS draw_pct, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN away_club_goals > home_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS away_win_pct FROM games WHERE competition_id = 'GB1' AND season = 2020 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

executed_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN attendance IS NULL THEN 'empty (NULL attendance)' ELSE 'real crowd (attendance present)' END AS crowd_bucket, COUNT(*) AS match_count, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals > away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS home_win_pct, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN home_club_goals = away_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS draw_pct, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN away_club_goals > home_club_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS away_win_pct FROM games WHERE competition_id = 'GB1' AND season = 2020 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 1000
results.conclusion: With attendance-empty defined correctly as NULL, the 2020 Premier League splits cleanly into 349 fan-less matches and 31 with a real crowd. The empty bucket shows the inversion directly — away wins at 41.26% edge out home wins at 36.39% — while the 31 crowded matches retain a strong, normal home advantage of 54.84% home vs 29.03% away. Because empty games make up roughly 92% of the season, the empty-bucket behaviour drives the full-season inversion. This is the direct, side-by-side evidence you asked for and it squarely attributes the 2020 collapse in home advantage to the absence of crowds.

results.targets: the 31 crowded matches used as the normal-home-advantage comparison
results.question: Hold on — those 31 crowded matches almost certainly aren't scattered through 2020, they're the pre-lockdown fixtures from the start of the season. Pull the match dates for both buckets and confirm whether the crowded games are just a time window rather than a fair comparison against the empty ones.

plan.intent: Headline date span of each attendance bucket
plan.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN attendance IS NULL THEN 'empty (NULL attendance)' ELSE 'real crowd (attendance present)' END AS crowd_bucket, COUNT(*) AS match_count, MIN(date) AS first_match_date, MAX(date) AS last_match_date FROM games WHERE competition_id = 'GB1' AND season = 2020 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

plan.intent: Monthly distribution of matches per bucket to expose clustering
plan.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', date) AS match_month, CASE WHEN attendance IS NULL THEN 'empty (NULL attendance)' ELSE 'real crowd (attendance present)' END AS crowd_bucket, COUNT(*) AS match_count FROM games WHERE competition_id = 'GB1' AND season = 2020 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

executed_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN attendance IS NULL THEN 'empty (NULL attendance)' ELSE 'real crowd (attendance present)' END AS crowd_bucket, COUNT(*) AS match_count, MIN(date) AS first_match_date, MAX(date) AS last_match_date FROM games WHERE competition_id = 'GB1' AND season = 2020 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 1000

SELECT DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', date) AS match_month, CASE WHEN attendance IS NULL THEN 'empty (NULL attendance)' ELSE 'real crowd (attendance present)' END AS crowd_bucket, COUNT(*) AS match_count FROM games WHERE competition_id = 'GB1' AND season = 2020 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2 LIMIT 1000
results.conclusion: The dates overturn the pre-lockdown theory rather than confirm it. The 2020 season (Sep 2020–May 2021) actually began with empty stadiums on 12 September 2020, and the first match with a real crowd did not occur until 5 December 2020 — so the crowded games cannot be start-of-season fixtures. Instead they fall into two later windows when spectators were briefly permitted: 14 games in December 2020 and 17 in May 2021, while every match from September–November 2020 and January–April 2021 was played behind closed doors. The crowd/empty contrast is therefore not distorted by an early-season timing bias, though it is still an observational comparison confined to two short periods rather than a fully randomised one.

results.targets: the 31 crowded matches as a fair comparison / club quality definition
results.question: Those 31 crowded games being confined to two short windows worries me about selection bias — the home teams allowed fans may just have been stronger sides. Check which clubs hosted those 31 matches and whether they skew toward strong home teams versus the empty bucket. And don't define 'strong' by that season's results — use a stable measure like squad market value or the prior season's league finish.

plan.intent: Identify the host clubs of the 31 crowded matches
plan.sql: SELECT home_club_name, COUNT(*) AS crowded_matches FROM games WHERE season = 2020 AND competition_id = 'GB1' AND attendance IS NOT NULL GROUP BY home_club_name ORDER BY crowded_matches DESC, home_club_name

plan.intent: Compare average home-club squad value between buckets
plan.sql: WITH latest_val AS (SELECT player_id, current_club_id, market_value_in_eur, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_id ORDER BY date DESC) AS rn FROM player_valuations WHERE date < DATE '2020-09-01'), club_value AS (SELECT current_club_id AS club_id, SUM(market_value_in_eur) AS squad_value FROM latest_val WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY current_club_id), gb AS (SELECT home_club_id, CASE WHEN attendance IS NULL THEN 'empty (NULL attendance)' ELSE 'real crowd (attendance present)' END AS crowd_bucket FROM games WHERE season = 2020 AND competition_id = 'GB1') SELECT gb.crowd_bucket, COUNT(*) AS match_count, ROUND(AVG(cv.squad_value), 2) AS avg_home_squad_value, ROUND(MEDIAN(cv.squad_value), 2) AS median_home_squad_value FROM gb JOIN club_value cv ON gb.home_club_id = cv.club_id GROUP BY gb.crowd_bucket ORDER BY gb.crowd_bucket

plan.intent: Club-by-club squad value with crowd vs empty match counts
plan.sql: WITH latest_val AS (SELECT player_id, current_club_id, market_value_in_eur, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_id ORDER BY date DESC) AS rn FROM player_valuations WHERE date < DATE '2020-09-01'), club_value AS (SELECT current_club_id AS club_id, SUM(market_value_in_eur) AS squad_value FROM latest_val WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY current_club_id) SELECT g.home_club_name, ROUND(cv.squad_value, 2) AS squad_value, SUM(CASE WHEN g.attendance IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS crowded_home_matches, SUM(CASE WHEN g.attendance IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS empty_home_matches FROM games g JOIN club_value cv ON g.home_club_id = cv.club_id WHERE g.season = 2020 AND g.competition_id = 'GB1' GROUP BY g.home_club_name, cv.squad_value ORDER BY cv.squad_value DESC

executed_sql: SELECT home_club_name, COUNT(*) AS crowded_matches FROM games WHERE season = 2020 AND competition_id = 'GB1' AND NOT attendance IS NULL GROUP BY home_club_name ORDER BY crowded_matches DESC, home_club_name LIMIT 1000

WITH latest_val AS (SELECT player_id, current_club_id, market_value_in_eur, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_id ORDER BY date DESC) AS rn FROM player_valuations WHERE date < CAST('2020-09-01' AS DATE)), club_value AS (SELECT current_club_id AS club_id, SUM(market_value_in_eur) AS squad_value FROM latest_val WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY current_club_id), gb AS (SELECT home_club_id, CASE WHEN attendance IS NULL THEN 'empty (NULL attendance)' ELSE 'real crowd (attendance present)' END AS crowd_bucket FROM games WHERE season = 2020 AND competition_id = 'GB1') SELECT gb.crowd_bucket, COUNT(*) AS match_count, ROUND(AVG(cv.squad_value), 2) AS avg_home_squad_value, ROUND(MEDIAN(cv.squad_value), 2) AS median_home_squad_value FROM gb JOIN club_value AS cv ON gb.home_club_id = cv.club_id GROUP BY gb.crowd_bucket ORDER BY gb.crowd_bucket LIMIT 1000

WITH latest_val AS (SELECT player_id, current_club_id, market_value_in_eur, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_id ORDER BY date DESC) AS rn FROM player_valuations WHERE date < CAST('2020-09-01' AS DATE)), club_value AS (SELECT current_club_id AS club_id, SUM(market_value_in_eur) AS squad_value FROM latest_val WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY current_club_id) SELECT g.home_club_name, ROUND(cv.squad_value, 2) AS squad_value, SUM(CASE WHEN NOT g.attendance IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS crowded_home_matches, SUM(CASE WHEN g.attendance IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS empty_home_matches FROM games AS g JOIN club_value AS cv ON g.home_club_id = cv.club_id WHERE g.season = 2020 AND g.competition_id = 'GB1' GROUP BY g.home_club_name, cv.squad_value ORDER BY cv.squad_value DESC LIMIT 1000
results.conclusion: Checking the 31 crowded matches against a stable squad-value measure, there is only a mild lean toward stronger home sides — crowded-bucket hosts averaged €315.3m in squad value versus €294.9m for empty-bucket hosts (~7% higher; medians €261.3m vs €251.6m, ~4%). Crucially, the crowded games are spread across 18 of the 20 clubs and include plenty of weaker sides (West Brom €84.5m, Southampton €113.3m, Brighton €123.3m, Chelsea €142.6m), while some strong clubs like Aston Villa (€472.3m) hosted no crowded games at all. This does not look like a strong-team selection bias large enough to manufacture the observed 54.84%/29.03% home advantage in the crowded bucket, so the crowd-effect interpretation survives this check — though the comparison remains observational and I could only apply the squad-value proxy, not the requested prior-season league finish.

results.targets: the squad-value-only 'strong home team' check that omitted prior-season league finish
results.question: You dodged the prior-season league finish part — do that now: rank the crowded-bucket hosts versus the empty-bucket hosts by where each club finished in the 2019 season table, and tell me if the crowded hosts skew toward top-half finishers.

plan.intent: Headline: compare buckets on average 2019 finish and top-half share
plan.sql: WITH standings AS (SELECT home_club_id AS club_id, date, home_club_position AS pos FROM games WHERE season=2019 AND competition_id='GB1' AND home_club_position IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT away_club_id, date, away_club_position FROM games WHERE season=2019 AND competition_id='GB1' AND away_club_position IS NOT NULL), ranked AS (SELECT club_id, pos AS finish_2019, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY club_id ORDER BY date DESC) rn FROM standings), final_pos AS (SELECT club_id, finish_2019 FROM ranked WHERE rn=1), matches AS (SELECT home_club_id, CASE WHEN attendance IS NULL THEN 'empty (NULL attendance)' ELSE 'real crowd' END AS bucket FROM games WHERE season=2020 AND competition_id='GB1') SELECT m.bucket, COUNT(*) AS match_count, ROUND(AVG(fp.finish_2019),2) AS avg_2019_finish, ROUND(100.0*AVG(CASE WHEN fp.finish_2019<=10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),2) AS pct_top_half_2019, SUM(CASE WHEN fp.finish_2019 IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matches_host_no_2019_finish FROM matches m LEFT JOIN final_pos fp ON m.home_club_id=fp.club_id GROUP BY m.bucket ORDER BY m.bucket

plan.intent: Per-club detail: each host's 2019 finish with crowded vs empty home-match counts
plan.sql: WITH standings AS (SELECT home_club_id AS club_id, date, home_club_position AS pos FROM games WHERE season=2019 AND competition_id='GB1' AND home_club_position IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT away_club_id, date, away_club_position FROM games WHERE season=2019 AND competition_id='GB1' AND away_club_position IS NOT NULL), ranked AS (SELECT club_id, pos AS finish_2019, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY club_id ORDER BY date DESC) rn FROM standings), final_pos AS (SELECT club_id, finish_2019 FROM ranked WHERE rn=1), m AS (SELECT home_club_id, home_club_name, attendance FROM games WHERE season=2020 AND competition_id='GB1') SELECT m.home_club_name, fp.finish_2019 AS finish_2019, SUM(CASE WHEN m.attendance IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS crowded_home_matches, SUM(CASE WHEN m.attendance IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS empty_home_matches FROM m LEFT JOIN final_pos fp ON m.home_club_id=fp.club_id GROUP BY m.home_club_name, fp.finish_2019 ORDER BY fp.finish_2019 NULLS LAST

executed_sql: WITH standings AS (SELECT home_club_id AS club_id, date, home_club_position AS pos FROM games WHERE season = 2019 AND competition_id = 'GB1' AND NOT home_club_position IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT away_club_id, date, away_club_position FROM games WHERE season = 2019 AND competition_id = 'GB1' AND NOT away_club_position IS NULL), ranked AS (SELECT club_id, pos AS finish_2019, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY club_id ORDER BY date DESC) AS rn FROM standings), final_pos AS (SELECT club_id, finish_2019 FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1), matches AS (SELECT home_club_id, CASE WHEN attendance IS NULL THEN 'empty (NULL attendance)' ELSE 'real crowd' END AS bucket FROM games WHERE season = 2020 AND competition_id = 'GB1') SELECT m.bucket, COUNT(*) AS match_count, ROUND(AVG(fp.finish_2019), 2) AS avg_2019_finish, ROUND(100.0 * AVG(CASE WHEN fp.finish_2019 <= 10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 2) AS pct_top_half_2019, SUM(CASE WHEN fp.finish_2019 IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matches_host_no_2019_finish FROM matches AS m LEFT JOIN final_pos AS fp ON m.home_club_id = fp.club_id GROUP BY m.bucket ORDER BY m.bucket LIMIT 1000

WITH standings AS (SELECT home_club_id AS club_id, date, home_club_position AS pos FROM games WHERE season = 2019 AND competition_id = 'GB1' AND NOT home_club_position IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT away_club_id, date, away_club_position FROM games WHERE season = 2019 AND competition_id = 'GB1' AND NOT away_club_position IS NULL), ranked AS (SELECT club_id, pos AS finish_2019, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY club_id ORDER BY date DESC) AS rn FROM standings), final_pos AS (SELECT club_id, finish_2019 FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1), m AS (SELECT home_club_id, home_club_name, attendance FROM games WHERE season = 2020 AND competition_id = 'GB1') SELECT m.home_club_name, fp.finish_2019 AS finish_2019, SUM(CASE WHEN NOT m.attendance IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS crowded_home_matches, SUM(CASE WHEN m.attendance IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS empty_home_matches FROM m LEFT JOIN final_pos AS fp ON m.home_club_id = fp.club_id GROUP BY m.home_club_name, fp.finish_2019 ORDER BY fp.finish_2019 LIMIT 1000
results.conclusion: Ranking the hosts by their 2019 final league position shows no meaningful skew of the crowded-bucket games toward strong sides, and specifically no lean toward top-half finishers. The crowded hosts averaged a 2019 finish of 8.78 versus 9.02 for empty-bucket hosts — a negligible ~0.24-place difference — and only 45.16% of crowded matches were hosted by 2019 top-half clubs, actually below the empty bucket's 50.43%. The 31 crowded games are drawn from across the table (champions Liverpool through 16th-placed West Ham, plus promoted sides), rather than concentrated among the elite. This directly answers the deferred prior-season-finish check and reinforces the squad-value result: the crowd/empty contrast is not distorted by a strong-team selection bias, so the crowd-effect interpretation of the 2020 home-advantage collapse survives.
